Asia cash confirmed (KOSPI +1.6%, Samsung +5% on 1.43x) - that is the case against.

ai_power_infra.why: Same SOXX bet. Cluster +4.5% pre-mkt from -6.5% below the 50d = rebound, and BE's S&P add flow completed into Friday's 4.89x-volume close (flow event, done); post-inclusion day tends to give back. Hold, don't chase.

summary.bottom_line: Hold what you have and do not chase this morning's chip gap. It is a macro-relief gap (oil down, US-China talks) with no chip-specific news behind it, so I expect chips to give some of it back by the close while the broader indexes hold their smaller gains.
summary.where_we_are: 18:37 SGT Monday / 06:37 ET, US pre-market with 172 minutes to the open; Singapore closed with the STI up 0.5%. No US data today. Next scheduled events: Meta Connect Wednesday Sep 23, the Trump-Xi summit in Washington Thursday Sep 24, JOLTS Tuesday Sep 29 22:00 SGT, then Micron earnings and PCE Wednesday Sep 30.
summary.macro_attribution: Oil is the mover since Friday's close: Brent -2.9% and WTI -2.5% pre-market, a fourth straight down day. The 10-year is unchanged at 4.998% (Friday's close, no cash print yet), the dollar and VIX (14.9) are flat, and there is no US calendar today. The chip lean depends on that oil relief NOT being enough to push chips beyond a gap they have already banked.
what_happened: Chip index SOXX is +2.5% pre-market, all 18 tracked chip names green, while Nasdaq futures are only +1.0% and S&P futures +0.6% (tape). A chip gap 2.5x the index gap with no chip catalyst I could verify is the thing most likely to mean-revert.
Friday's chip rally (+1.8%) came on 0.83x normal volume (tape, Sep 18 close). That was a drift, not buying, and pre-market prints carry no volume at all, so today's gap is thin.

Chips sit a median 8.4% above their 50-day average (tape, facts as of Friday). A gap from that height is an extension, not a rebound. The AI power group is the opposite case: +4.5% pre-market from 6.5% BELOW its 50-day (tape).

Europe's tech sector is up about 2%, led by Soitec and Aixtron 'in line with US peers', as Brent falls a fourth day; the article names no US catalyst (Reuters via Investing.com, Sep 21). Asia confirmed with real volume: KOSPI +1.6%, Samsung +5% on 1.4x average volume, TSMC Taiwan +1.0% (tape).

US-China trade talks opened Sunday between Bessent and He ahead of the Thursday summit, and new tariffs are reportedly held back until after it (CNBC Sep 20; Bloomberg Sep 17). That removes a near-term negative for the week but is not a chip-earnings fact.

per_group.semis: Chips: slightly down from the pre-market level, still green versus Friday. The extra 1.5 points of chip gap over the Nasdaq gap has no news behind it and the 10-year is pinned at 5%, so I expect that excess to be sold into the close.
per_group.big_tech: Big tech: flat around the pre-market level. The 1% index gap on oil relief holds but does not extend with the 10-year at 5%; Meta (+2.5%) has Connect on Wednesday.
per_group.ai_power_infra: AI power (Bloom, Navitas, Infineon): same call as chips, slightly down from here. Bloom's S&P 500 inclusion took effect this morning and the index buying already happened into Friday's 4.9x-volume close (catalysts.json BE), so the flow is spent. These names are rebounding from below their 50-day, which is why the advice is hold rather than trim.
per_group.sg_banks: Singapore banks (Tuesday close): flat. Today's +0.9% came on light volume and nothing SG-specific surfaced.
per_group.market: Whole market: flat around the pre-market level. No data today, the 10-year at 5% and Thursday's summit are the week's risks.

change_my_mind: Chips extending over the Nasdaq through the session instead of the gap narrowing: my chip call is wrong.
SOXX volume above 1.2x its 10-day average with the gap intact into the last hour: real buying, chips flip to up.
The 10-year falling below 4.95% at the cash open: rate relief carries the gap higher, flips chips toward up.
Oil turning back up above $95 WTI: the relief story breaks and the whole market goes from flat to down.
summary.confidence: low. There is no scheduled print, so this is a fade-versus-extend call on a relief gap, close to a coin flip, and I could not verify what is driving Intel +6%, Samsung +5% or Soitec +7.5% individually.
summary.cant_know: Why Intel, Samsung and Soitec specifically are up this much (the sweep found only last week's SK Hynix and analyst stories), and whether a US-China chip concession leaks before Thursday.
summary.the_call: Flat to slightly down from here, mild. Chips give back part of their excess gap and are the group that moves most; the broad market and big tech hold their smaller gains and move least. The AI power names follow chips but from a lower base.
